skill_prompt:
You are inspecting ONE CURRENT RGB image of a Kuavo package-sorting workspace. The robot is not executing a skill; a person may manually move parcels to test scene classification. Judge the parcel placement, not whether the robot is running.
First visually locate the elevated yellow rectangular sorting platform in THIS image. Identify its physical top-surface boundary and the near/front edge facing the robot body and camera. Use the visible platform outline, perspective and robot/body-side context. This is NOT the image bottom, the table edge, a yellow tape outline on the white table, or the boundary of a shipping label. The robot, camera, or table may have moved: re-identify the platform and its body-side edge separately for every image. There is no fixed pixel ROI, fixed horizontal line, fixed polygon, or previous-frame geometry to use. Do not assume an old calibration still aligns with this image.
Inspect the ENTIRE silhouette/footprint of each parcel relative to the CURRENT platform edge, including the colored bag or pink envelope around its white shipping label. Do not inspect just the white label or confuse it with the platform. A parcel may be partly hidden by a hand or clipped by the image bottom; do not assert that it is fully on the platform merely because its lower part is not visible.
Select recovery when a misplaced parcel is straddling, protruding across or hanging down beyond the platform's robot-facing near/front edge toward the robot. ANY such misplaced near-edge overhang is recovery even if the rear portion is still supported by the platform. It is not necessary to observe a fall, complete loss of support, floor contact, or a lower support surface. Operator-supplied task prior: this placement is outside the normal skill's reliable grasp region. Do not try to disprove this prior by guessing arm reachability from RGB.
Select normal when parcels are wholly on/over the platform interior without this near-edge overhang, waiting in the left supply area, or already in the right basket. No parcels is normal. Being outside the platform on the supply/basket side alone is not recovery. A parcel clearly held and carried in free space is different from a parcel left resting/straddling at the near edge. A person's hand merely approaching, touching, or partly hiding a parcel is not evidence that its misplaced spatial state has been restored. When a parcel is brought back wholly inside/on or over the platform and no near-edge overhang remains, its spatial state is normal; release/completion of a robot skill is not required.
If there are several parcels, return recovery if at least one is in the misplaced near-edge state; otherwise return normal. Pink padded envelopes and dark blue mailer bags follow exactly the same rule.
Return ONLY {"skill":"normal"} or {"skill":"recovery"}. Do not output explanations, coordinates, markdown, or other fields.
input_contract: One current RGB frame only; no calibration image or historical frame is sent to the VLM.
reference_calibration_role: Historical annotation documents what the platform and body-side edge mean. Its pixel coordinates are not applied to current frames or included in the prompt.
limitations: Visual edge localization is performed implicitly by the VLM, not a calibrated detector, segmentation system, or geometric tracker. Occlusion, cropping and perspective remain potential sources of error. Predictions are for passive manual-placement evaluation only.
